sections.h2: Where is Boise and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Boise is the capital of Idaho, built along the Boise River in the Treasure Valley of southwestern Idaho. The city was founded in 1863 and incorporated in 1864, and downtown sits at about 2,704 feet above sea level.

The city spreads out in several distinct areas. Wikipedia's list of Boise neighborhoods includes the North End, the Bench, Downtown, the Boise State University area, Boise Highlands, Warm Springs and the East End, Harris Ranch and Riverland East, plus Northwest, Southwest, Southeast and West Boise. Buyers will ask which part of town the house is in, so name the neighborhood first.

Wikipedia names the Boise School District and the West Ada School District as the school systems serving the area. Check the district boundary for your exact address before you describe the house to a buyer.

  • Founded 1863, incorporated 1864
  • Downtown elevation: 2,704 feet
  • Estimated population on July 1, 2025: 238,429 (Census Bureau)

sections.h2: What does Boise's economy mean for people selling a house?
sections.html:
Boise has a mixed economy built around technology, health care, education, government and food companies, and that mix shapes who is moving in and out of its homes. Wikipedia lists Micron Technology, Hewlett-Packard, St. Luke's Health System, Saint Alphonsus Regional Medical Center, West Ada School District, Boise State University, the Idaho Department of Health and Welfare, the City of Boise, J.R. Simplot, Boise Cascade, Lamb Weston and WinCo Foods among the largest employers in the area.

For sellers, a job move at one of these employers often brings a fixed moving date, and a seller who must be out by then may not be able to wait through a long listing period.

sections.h2: How do Boise's summers and winters affect a house?
sections.html:
Boise has a cool semi-arid climate, so the house has to handle hot dry summers and moderately cold winters. In a typical year the city reaches 100 degrees Fahrenheit on about nine days and 90 degrees on about 55 days. The December average is 32.1 degrees, and the temperature drops to 0 degrees or lower on roughly one night a year.

Precipitation is low, about 12 inches a year, and snowfall averages 18 inches or less. The record low is minus 28 degrees, set January 16, 1888. For a seller, that range turns attention to a short list of items:

  • Air conditioning age and condition, since cooling runs hard from June through August
  • Roof surface and attic ventilation under long dry heat
  • Exposed pipes and hose bibs on the few nights each winter that fall to zero

A cash buyer prices these items in, which is one reason a house with an old air conditioner or a worn roof can sell as-is without a repair list.

sections.h2: Does Boise's wildland urban interface overlay affect a sale?
sections.html:
It can, if the house sits in the foothills or another area the city has mapped as higher wildfire risk. The City of Boise has a Wildland Urban Interface Overlay, known as the WUI-O, meant to reduce risk to life and property in areas with higher wildfire risk.

The overlay applies to all new structures and additions built after its effective date. It also reaches renovations of existing buildings that increase gross floor area by more than 49 percent. Areas that generally include the foothills fire hazard zone use Class 1 Ignition-Resistant Construction, called IR1, while valley and desert areas use Class 2, called IR2. The city says IR1 areas will grow with annexation, generally north and west of Hill Road.

Interior renovations are not covered unless they come with exterior changes that pass the 49 percent mark. A seller with a foothills house who plans to enlarge it before listing should talk to the city planning department first, because an addition can bring the ignition-resistant rules into play. A seller who simply sells the house as it stands is not asked to rebuild it.

sections.h2: What disclosure does an Idaho seller owe a buyer in Boise?
sections.html:
Idaho requires most sellers of residential property to complete a property condition disclosure form. Section 55-2504 of the Idaho Code says anyone who intends to transfer residential real property, including non-owner-occupied rental property, must complete the applicable items on the form prescribed under section 55-2508.

Section 55-2509 then requires the buyer to sign and date a copy and return it. The Idaho Legislature lists many exemptions in section 55-2505, and several of them come up often among Boise sellers:

  • A transfer by a fiduciary during the administration of a decedent's estate, a guardianship, a conservatorship or a trust
  • A transfer from a decedent's estate, or one ordered by a probate court
  • A transfer by foreclosure sale, or by deed in lieu of foreclosure
  • A transfer to a spouse or to a lineal relative, or between co-owners
  • A transfer from a seller who has not lived in the home within the last year and who got it through inheritance or devise

If your sale fits one of those categories, the form may not be required, but a buyer can still ask about the property's condition. This page gives general information, so confirm your situation with an Idaho real estate attorney or a title company.

sections.h2: How do Ada County taxes and recording work when a Boise house sells?
sections.html:
Boise sits in Ada County, so the county assessor values the house, the county treasurer bills the tax, and the county recorder records the deed. Each year the assessor estimates what a typical buyer would pay for your property as of January 1, and the assessor usually mails assessment notices by the first Monday in June.

Property tax bills go out by the fourth Monday in November. Ada County lists December 20 as the due date for the full-year payment or the first half, with the second half due June 20. The Idaho State Tax Commission says you can appeal your assessed value to the county Board of Equalization by the fourth Monday in June, and a further appeal must be filed within 30 days with the State Board of Tax Appeals or the district court.

The Tax Commission example for a homeowner's exemption shows a reduction of $125,000 in taxable value. Idaho sets no legal limit on how much one property's tax bill can change, though each taxing district can raise the property tax part of its budget by no more than 3 percent unless voters approve more or new construction applies. Your closing agent will split the year's tax between you and the buyer, so ask for the numbers early.

sections.h2: What changed with Boise short-term rentals?
sections.html:
The City of Boise no longer requires a short-term rental license. On May 12, 2026 the City Council approved repealing the ordinance to match changes in Idaho state law, and the repeal took effect on May 18, 2026.

Existing licenses stayed valid through May 18, 2026. The city says it will keep enforcing nuisance, noise, parking, safety and occupancy rules that are consistent with state law and city code. Idaho's Senate Bill 1162 of 2025 also changed section 67-6539 of the Idaho Code so that a city or county may not adopt or enforce an ordinance that has the express or practical effect of prohibiting short-term rentals.

If you own a house that has been used as a short-term rental, the practical effect is simple: the buyer is no longer buying a city license along with the house. You should still gather booking records, platform tax filings and any homeowners association rules before you list, because buyers and lenders ask about rental history.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense for a Boise house?
sections.html:
A cash sale makes sense when time, condition or paperwork would make a normal listing slow or costly. Sellers in Boise commonly look at a cash offer for these situations:

  • An inherited house that no heir wants to maintain
  • A house needing a roof, cooling or foundation work the owner cannot fund
  • A rental with a tenant in place or a vacant unit with city code issues
  • A job or health change that sets a firm moving date

Cash Home Buyers makes offers on houses as they stand, with no commissions and no closing costs to the seller on our side. You decide whether to accept, and declining costs nothing. Compare any offer with what a listing would net after repairs, commission and carrying costs.

faqs.q: How big is Boise and when did it become a city?
faqs.a: Boise had an estimated 238,429 residents on July 1, 2025 according to the Census Bureau. It was founded in 1863 and incorporated in 1864.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due on a Boise house?
faqs.a: Ada County's first-half payment is due December 20 and the second half is due June 20. The assessor usually mails assessment notices by the first Monday in June, and appeals to the Board of Equalization are due by the fourth Monday in June.

faqs.q: Do I need a short-term rental license to sell a Boise house that was an Airbnb?
faqs.a: No. Boise repealed its short-term rental license requirement effective May 18, 2026. The city still enforces nuisance, noise, parking, safety and occupancy rules.

faqs.q: Do I have to fill out a disclosure form when selling a house in Boise?
faqs.a: Usually yes. Idaho Code 55-2504 requires a property condition disclosure for residential transfers, but section 55-2505 exempts several transfers, including those by a fiduciary in an estate and foreclosure sales.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Boise foothills house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. The wildland urban interface overlay applies to new structures and to additions or renovations above 49 percent of floor area. A sale of an existing house as it stands does not trigger a rebuild, though you should confirm details with the city.
